intelligence.essence: The fix-17 checker's own byte-check script printed the wrong shas for the COVER_DAY and WISDOM arrays — its lazy regex grabbed the declaration prefix and stopped at the first `];` — and its `renderMonth found: false` was the same regex missing the loop's exact spacing. The checker did not pass those readings through: it re-extracted both arrays with a bracket-balanced parse, matched the maker's shas exactly, and proved the month grid by render. When your own harness mis-measures, re-prove the measurement — never let a tool's misreading stand as a verdict, for or against.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you measured your toy with a stretchy ruler, sweetheart, and it said the toy was the wrong size! But the ruler was wrong, sweetheart — not the toy! So we measure it again with a good ruler, sweetheart, and then we know for sure!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — the checker's little measuring tool read the numbers wrong, dear, because of how it grabbed the text, and it even said a part wasn't there when it was. But the checker didn't just believe the tool, love — it measured again properly, and everything matched. So when your own tool gives you a strange answer, dear, you check the tool before you blame the thing you're measuring.
